questions.question_text: Trace the deletion of a node with two children in a Binary Search Tree containing the sequence of insertions [50, 30, 70, 20, 40, 60, 80] by applying the inorder successor rule, and calculate the final inorder traversal sequence of the resulting tree.

Implement the deletion of a node having a single child in a Binary Search Tree containing keys [40, 20, 60, 50], and compute the resulting sequence after performing an inorder traversal on the updated tree.

solutions.model_answer: Inserting the sequence [50, 30, 70, 20, 40, 60, 80] forms a BST with root 50, left child 30 (with children 20 and 40), and right child 70 (with children 60 and 80). To delete root node 50 which has two children, Case 3 applies: replace 50 with its inorder successor, which is the minimum key in its right subtree (60). Removing original 65/60 and placing 60 at the root preserves the BST invariant. The final inorder traversal visiting Left, Root, Right in ascending order yields: 20, 30, 40, 60, 70, 80.

marking_scheme.criterion: Constructs the initial BST structure correctly from the insertion sequence [50, 30, 70, 20, 40, 60, 80]
Identifies the node with two children (50) and applies the inorder successor rule (minimum key in the right subtree: 60)
Calculates and states the correct final inorder traversal sequence: 20, 30, 40, 60, 70, 80

solutions.model_answer: Inserting keys [40, 20, 60, 50] creates a BST with root 40, left child 20, and right child 60 which has a single left child 50. To delete node 60 having a single child, Case 2 applies: the node is replaced by its child (50). The updated tree has root 40, left child 20, and right child 50. Performing an inorder traversal (Left, Root, Right) on the updated tree visits the keys in strictly ascending order: 20, 40, 50.

marking_scheme.criterion: Constructs the initial BST structure correctly from the keys [40, 20, 60, 50]
Identifies the node with a single child (60) and replaces it with its child (50) per Case 2

questions.question_text: Analyze a relation scheme exhibiting transitive and partial dependencies, and decompose it into relations satisfying BCNF while ensuring lossless-join and dependency preservation properties.

solutions.model_answer: To analyze and decompose the relation scheme, first identify partial dependencies (where a non-prime attribute depends on a proper subset of a candidate key) and transitive dependencies (where a non-prime attribute depends on another non-prime attribute) violating 2NF and 3NF. BCNF is achieved by ensuring that for every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y, X must be a superkey. Decomposition must be performed step-by-step to eliminate these violations while testing and maintaining the lossless-join property and dependency preservation property.

questions.question_text: Explain the three-way handshake process for establishing a TCP connection and describe how the congestion window (cwnd) behaves during the Slow Start and Congestion Avoidance phases.

solutions.model_answer: The three-way handshake establishes a reliable full-duplex TCP connection as follows: (1) the client sends a SYN packet with an initial sequence number ISN_c; (2) the server replies with a SYN+ACK packet acknowledging ISN_c+1 and sending its own initial sequence number ISN_s; (3) the client sends an ACK packet acknowledging ISN_s+1. Regarding congestion control, the congestion window (cwnd) behaves as follows: during Slow Start, cwnd starts small and increases by 1 MSS per ACK (doubling roughly every RTT) until it reaches ssthresh; during Congestion Avoidance, cwnd grows linearly by approximately 1 MSS per RTT through Additive Increase.

marking_scheme.criterion: Explains step 1 of the three-way handshake (client sends SYN with ISN_c)
Explains step 2 of the three-way handshake (server replies with SYN+ACK acknowledging ISN_c+1 and sending ISN_s)
Explains step 3 of the three-way handshake (client sends ACK acknowledging ISN_s+1)
Describes Slow Start behavior of cwnd (starts small, increases by 1 MSS per ACK, doubling roughly every RTT up to ssthresh)
Describes Congestion Avoidance behavior of cwnd (grows linearly by approximately 1 MSS per RTT via Additive Increase)
